title: Minimal extension permissions with activeTab and optional grants
when: A browser extension asks for broad access and the user wants fewer install warnings, an easier review and less risk, while keeping every feature working.
prompt:
Goal: A manifest that requests only what each feature uses, relies on activeTab for user triggered actions and asks for the rest at runtime.
Steps:
1. List each feature and its API calls, map every call to a permission, and delete permissions no call needs.
2. Prefer "activeTab": a click on the action, a context menu item or a command grants temporary access to the current tab, with no install warning.
3. Pair "activeTab" with "scripting" to inject code on click instead of content_scripts on every site.
4. Skip "tabs" when you only need the active tab id or tabs.query; it is for reading url and title of other tabs.
5. Rare features: "optional_permissions": ["downloads"] and "optional_host_permissions": ["https://api.example.com/*"]; call chrome.permissions.request inside a click handler and check permissions.contains before use.
6. chrome.permissions.remove drops a grant when its feature is switched off.
7. PERMISSIONS.md lists each permission, its feature and the warning users see; reuse the text for store justifications.
Quality bar:
- Each permission has a one line reason.
- A refused optional grant degrades politely.
Pitfalls:
- <all_urls> or *://*/* just in case.
- permissions.request outside a user gesture, which fails.
- A new permission in an update, which disables the extension until users accept.
Verify:
- [ ] No <all_urls> anywhere.
- [ ] Each permission in PERMISSIONS.md.
- [ ] Optional grants requested from a click.
- [ ] manifest.json is valid JSON.
Output: Updated manifest.json and PERMISSIONS.md.

examples.input: minha extensao pede acesso a todos os sites, da para reduzir?
examples.output: manifest with activeTab plus scripting, optional host permission requested on click, tabs removed, PERMISSIONS.md with reasons and warnings
